chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Hamzah al-Qummi from Zakariyya ibn Adam who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: "I forbid you from the slaughtered meat of everyone who is upon opposition to what you and your companions are upon, except in the time of necessity for it." And the second aspect is that these narrations came down due to precaution (taqiyyah), because whoever opposes us permits eating the slaughtered meat of those who opposed Islam from the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimmah), and that which indicates this is what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of non-Shia Muslims according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prohibits consuming the meat of those differing in creed from the Shia, a ruling often interpreted through the lens of *taqiyyah* (precaution) to distinguish Shia practice from opposing sects who permitted eating the meat of the People of the Book. This distinction highlights the jurisprudential nuance in *tahdhib al-Ahkam*, where the prohibition serves not only as a theological boundary but also as a social marker of identity during periods of political tension.
